en: The Scripture of the One-Syllable Heart Mantra of the Great Dhāraṇī for the Age of Dharma, translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of India during the Great Tang Dynasty by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was dwelling in the palace of the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven, amidst inconceivable varieties...
He dwells amidst all the assemblies of bodhisattvas adorned with various ornaments,
as well as among the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and others, including the lunar mansions, celestial sages, and ṛṣis.
All of these were bodhisattvas of the tenth stage who had manifested through skillful means and were present in this assembly.
At that time, the World-Honored One sat within the Lotus Treasury Realm.
Observing the great assembly of devas, rishis, and others,
and desiring to benefit all sentient beings in the future degenerate age,
he entered the samādhi of the supreme Great Wheel-Turning King’s Crown of all Tathāgatas.
Immediately, he emitted a great light from between his eyebrows.
That light pervaded all Buddha-fields throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Among them, all sentient beings who encountered this light—
All were filled with joy.
Having pervaded everywhere, the light returned to the place where the Buddha was,
circled him three times, and entered the crown of the Tathāgata’s head.
Upon entering, various signs of adornment appeared once more.
Within that light, a voice suddenly spoke, saying:
"I am the One-Syllable Mantra of the Great Cakravartin King."
Surrounded by the respectful attendance of immeasurable celestial seers (*ṛṣi*),
a voice then emerged from within the light, saying:
"O Tathāgata Śākyamuni, I am the Single-Syllable Heart Mantra of all Tathāgatas, the Wheel-Turning King of Wisdom."
"O Ratnacchattra Buddha, among all the Buddhas of the past, present,
and future, I am the supreme secret heart-mantra."
Śālarāja Buddha, Amitābha Buddha, and Anabhibhūta Buddha.
Buddha Wondrous Eye,
Buddha Wondrous Banner,
Buddha Flower King.
All those Buddhas have universally proclaimed it;
all the immeasurable Buddhas of the past likewise rejoice in it.
You should now, for the sake of future sentient beings, [proclaim it as well].
He expounded this dhāraṇī so that all sentient beings might obtain great benefit.
At that time, having seen and heard this, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly.
"You all should know what is called the 'Single-Syllable Cakravartin King Mantra.
It is spoken as follows: [Mantra].

This is the single-syllable mantra from the Sanskrit original; the characters 'Lin' (upper tone) and 'Lin' (departing tone) are the Tang-dynasty pronunciation, which should be articulated with the tongue curled back. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha..."
He further addressed the assembly of devas and rishis:
"Listen attentively, all of you!
This dhāraṇī of the youth Mañjuśrī..."
I now wish to explain the maṇḍala rite, the recitation rite, and the fire-offering rite, which swiftly bring about accomplishment.
If there is anyone who can uphold this most excellent and wondrous dharani, [they shall attain success].
If you do not know the auspicious days, the various stars, and so forth,
O celestial deities, do not create obstacles.
If there is anyone capable of practicing my teachings, [grant them success].
You hosts of devas should protect and sustain this person;
all ghosts, spirits, and various malevolent vināyakas shall likewise provide guardianship and not cause them harm.
He protected and sustained them through skillful means,
causing them to give rise to faith and understanding within the teaching of the Ten Powers.
Having spoken these words, he immediately entered samādhi.
This is called the Samādhi Born from the Crown of All Tathāgatas,
which eliminates the unwholesome karma of all sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered that samādhi.
The Buddhas of the ten directions observed the Tathāgata residing in the Pure Celestial Palace;
one by one, they all came to assemble there.

Each requested Śākyamuni Buddha to proclaim a mantra, and they spoke these verses. Regarding the first phrase of the verses, "The Buddha speaks of Great Majestic Virtue" (*mahāvīrya*), the Tripiṭaka Master states that in the Sanskrit original it says "speaks" (*bhāṣate*); however, because the scribe-translator did not follow the local linguistic conventions, he rendered it as "the Buddha speaks."
The Buddha spoke of this Great Majestic Virtue, Which, for the benefit of all sentient beings,
can accomplish all mantras; May all aspirations be fulfilled—
This majestic power of the King of Mantras has been proclaimed by all Buddhas.
Among all mantras, this single syllable is the most honored and supreme;
born from the crown of the head, it possesses great majestic power. Its strength is inconceivable;
it effectively eliminates all demons and malevolent spirits, and repels all evil constellations.
The poisonous and harmful mother goddesses, as well as those nāgas and yakṣas of evil vows who afflict sentient beings— by reciting and upholding [this],
one shall obtain peace and happiness in the midst of the future degenerate age.
"Excellent, Teacher of Gods and Humans! We pray that you will speak for the sake of sentient beings.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions, having spoken these verses, remained silent.
At that time, all the places where sentient beings dwell throughout the trichiliocosm were suddenly enveloped in great flames,
their majestic radiance blazing with brilliant splendor.
Yet not a single class of sentient beings was harmed.

At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni surveyed all the pure celestial palaces and addressed the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, celestial seers, and the great multitude, saying:
Listen attentively, and I shall speak in verse:
I address all you sons of the Buddha: Listen well now;
I shall now proclaim this mantra, Which is endowed with all meritorious qualities.
In the evil age of the future, when my Dharma is about to perish,
you shall be able during that time to protect and uphold my Final Dharma;
you shall be able to eliminate the evils of the world and the malevolent spirits who cause harm.
As well as all gods, Māras, and humans— should they hear the name of this dhāraṇī,
all their various incantations and rites will be spontaneously crushed and subdued.
After my parinirvāṇa, once the relics have been distributed, [this shall likewise prevail].
One should conceal all the marks and signs and manifest this body through transformation.
This Buddha of the mantra has two kinds of bodies: the true body and the transformation body.
If one can make offerings to either, the merit and virtue are no different.
This mantra is likewise so: all devas and humans who are able to give rise to a mind of rare wonder, and who receive, uphold, and make offerings to it,
shall obtain all manner of meritorious virtues no different from my own body.
I have now briefly explained the merits of this King of Mantras.
At that time, having spoken these verses,
the World-Honored One expounded for the assembled multitude this Dharma of the Tathāgata’s Uṣṇīṣa of the Wheel-Turning King.
It can cause the dharmas of others to be swiftly destroyed,
and it can cause one's own dharmas to be swiftly accomplished;
it is universally praised by all bodhisattvas.
Within a radius of five hundred *yojanas* in the four directions of the place where one recites and contemplates [this],
all malevolent spirits shall naturally disperse and flee.
All mantra-practitioners who perform their own fundamental rites shall be utterly destroyed upon hearing this mantra;
all the supernatural powers (ṛddhi) possessed by all the devas shall likewise be completely lost.
Whether that mantra-holder wishes to extinguish another’s dharma or not to extinguish it,
it depends upon the mental focus maintained by that mantra-holder;
[this applies] to all mantra-holders, both mundane and supramundane.
Furthermore, there are no malevolent stars that it does not crush and subdue.
Whether for a son of good family who seeks to protect the Mahāyāna, or for his own sake, or in the face of an enemy; [this shall be accomplished].
One should take a handful of green grass in the hand,
recite the mantra one hundred and eight times,
and while harboring anger toward that person, cut the grass with a knife.
If one contemplates the destruction of that dharma, it will immediately be severed and destroyed.
If one wishes to cause the mantra-dhāraṇī of another person not to succeed,
one should recite the mantra seven times while forming a fist with the hand.
If one’s intention is directed toward another person, it will not be accomplished.
However, if one wishes for that other person to achieve success,
one simply opens one's fist, and it returns to its former state.
If one wishes to perform this rite,
one must first bathe and don fresh, clean garments;
then the rite itself will be accomplished.
If one wishes to protect others so that no evil spirits dare approach them,
one should recite this mantra; it shall protect oneself, protect others, and guard against both summoned spirits and those sent by others.
For all endeavors one seeks, this mantra shall be employed.
If one recites various other mantras without obtaining divine efficacy,
one should recite this mantra one million times.
One will immediately attain the accomplishment of the desired realm;
if there is no efficacy, the deity shall be extinguished on the spot.
If one desires for the celestial deity to come and serve as an attendant, [one should proceed accordingly].
One should take sesame oil, ghee, honey, and curd, mixing them together.
Taking a small pinch of the mixture, recite the mantra once and cast it into the fire once;
perform this one hundred and eight times until the burning is complete.
Within seven days, by performing this three times a day,
that deity will immediately come as a messenger.
If one wishes to subjugate the various devas, [one should proceed as follows].
Take one hundred and eight pieces of *devadāru* wood;
reciting the mantra over each one, cast them into the fire.
If you wish to summon a deity, [do so].
Recite their names,
performing the ritual three times a day for seven days;
they will swiftly descend and submit.
If one wishes to subjugate nāga maidens,
one should take ghee, honey, and milk,
and recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times three times a day while burning them as an oblation in the fire.
Within seven days, one will attain accomplishment.
If one wishes to summon yakṣas and yakṣiṇīs,
follow the previous ritual exactly to take curd-rice and burn it as an offering.
One will then achieve accomplishment.
If one wishes to subjugate a gandharva and his daughter,
one should burn all types of incense and, following the previous ritual method, burn various kinds of flowers.
All eight classes of goddesses will immediately descend and submit.
If one wishes to subjugate a true Brahmin,
one should take fine fragrant flowers and white mustard seeds, following exactly the previous ritual method.
One will immediately obtain one's wishes.
If one desires to subjugate a *rākṣasa*, one should take curd,
milk, and ghee, following the previous ritual procedure exactly as before.
One will then achieve success.
If one wishes to subjugate a guhyaka,
take ghee and earth, mix them together, and proceed according to the previous method.
If one wishes to subdue all evil persons and malevolent stars and constellations,
one should take ghee and sesame seeds and burn them according to the aforementioned ritual,
as described above.
Within seven days, by burning medicinal herbs at the three periods of the day, bathing, and reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times, one shall attain accomplishment.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken these words, [remained silent].
"O Mañjuśrī, the dhāraṇī-mantra you have taught possesses such power as described above.
In the future, during the final age..."
This Dharma enables all sentient beings to receive, uphold, practice, and apply it.
Furthermore, there are various other Dharmas which I shall now briefly explain.
Having spoken these words, [he remained silent].
At that time, the World-Honored One remained silent.
Then the fourfold assembly addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One, we pray that out of compassion you will further expound other teachings."
For the sake of bringing peace and happiness to future sentient beings,
at that time, Śākyamuni Buddha once again surveyed the pure celestial palaces.
He addressed the youth Mañjuśrī, saying:
"Listen well as I now briefly explain the rite for the one-syllable Wheel-Turning King’s mantra of majestic power and the method for painting its image,
for the sake of sentient beings in this degenerate age who possess little diligence and little wisdom."
For those who are unable to uphold the method for painting extensive images,
I shall now briefly explain the method for painting images,
desiring to bring benefit to all sentient beings.
Because it brings about the swift attainment of auspiciousness,
those who wish to uphold this most supreme Dharma should take a new piece of white cotton cloth, one zhang long and six chi wide, with its threads still uncut.
Do not use glue as a pigment for the colors.
The artist should bathe in fragrant water, don fresh and clean garments, and observe the eight precepts.
He should then paint the World-Honored One in the likeness of a Wheel-Turning King (cakravartin), with the countenance of one preaching the Dharma.
Beneath the seat of the Lord of All Worlds, paint the Holy Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva Brahmā; above the Buddha, paint the Devaputra Puṣpamāla raining flowers;
and beneath the seat, paint the Dharma-holders.
At that time, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni again looked upon the youth Mañjuśrī and addressed him, saying:
"Listen attentively, youth Mañjuśrī."
The Great Majestic Power of the Single-Syllable Wheel-Turning King:
I shall now briefly explain the method for painting his image,
so that sentient beings in this degenerate age may attain peace and happiness.
If one wishes to perform the ritual,
one should hold a censer in hand and gaze intently at the face of the Buddha,
ensuring that the face of the image is directed toward the west.
Having first made various offerings of incense and flowers,
the practitioner of the Dharma shall burn aloeswood incense three times each day,
facing the Buddha image and reciting this divine mantra.
After completing one million recitations, one may then perform the ritual.
The practitioner of this dharma must maintain the precepts and must always consume the "three white foods."
Regarding milk, curd, and non-glutinous rice:
one must not break the fast.
One should give rise to a mind of compassion toward all sentient beings and uphold the Bodhisattva precepts.
Whatever meritorious deeds this person desires to perform, as well as the healing of all diseases,
shall all be accomplished according to their wishes.
They must always make offerings to the Triple Gem.
If one wishes to accomplish the wheel rite,
one should fashion a wheel from iron;
that wheel shall have two hubs.
Erect a square altar before an image of the Buddha.
From the first day of the month until the fifteenth,
bathe three times daily and burn aloeswood incense.
Recite the mantra until it reaches one million times.
Regularly use various flowers as offerings.
On the fifteenth day, construct another altar once again.
Place the wheel in the center and cover it with both hands.
Recite the mantra with a sincere mind until the wheel manifests flames of light.
The practitioner who maintains this shall be able to ascend into the void and become a lord of the sages among the vidyādharas.
If others see this, they too will be able to soar through the air.
If one wishes to accomplish the parasol rite,
one should fashion a new white parasol.
Adorned with various kinds of gold, silver, and precious objects,
a single banner was suspended within it.
Holding the parasol in his hand, he recited the mantra exactly according to the previous method.
Immediately fire will emerge.
The practitioner who maintains the rite shall then soar into the void, as described above.
If one wishes to perform the ritual:
One should select the fifteenth day of the waxing moon and the five festival days, namely:
the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days of the month, as well as the twenty-third day and the final day of the month.
If one attains transformation of the body, one will certainly achieve accomplishment within fifteen days.
If this accomplishment is attained, all dharmas will likewise be accomplished.
One attains all supernatural powers (*abhijñā*) and all the dharmas of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
In this world, one becomes a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*) surrounded by a thousand sons.
If one wishes to perform the *uṣṇīṣa* rite, [one should proceed as follows].
Using gold, silver, copper, or tin, [fashion] an object the size of one's palm.
Recite the mantra over it according to the aforementioned method, as one would for the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa.
If a flame emerges from the crown of one's head, one will immediately attain the power of soaring through the air and preach the Dharma to all sentient beings for the duration of one great kalpa.
If one wishes to accomplish the rite of the wish-fulfilling vase (*cintāmaṇi-ghaṭa*), [one should proceed as follows].
One should fashion a single golden flask and fill it with all kinds of grain seeds, all kinds of medicinal seeds, and various precious objects.
The flask should be covered with a clean, white cotton cloth.
Beginning on the first day of the twelfth lunar month, recite the mantra;
within one year, you will attain accomplishment.
Whatever items are required from the flask will never be exhausted, even as they are constantly taken.
If one wishes to obtain a wish-fulfilling gem—
whether it be gold, precious jewels, or crystal— one should,
in accordance with the previous ritual, spread [the cloth] over it.
If one recites the mantra for one year,
one will swiftly attain accomplishment and achieve all that is sought,
whether among the gods or among humans.
Holding this jewel, one immediately becomes a Wheel-Turning King.
By reciting the mantra ten million times before that image,
one will immediately ascend into the void and attain a lifespan of one great kalpa.
If one wishes to accomplish the rite of the vajra,
one should fashion a single vajra from red sandalwood;
if red sandalwood is unavailable, an iron rod may also be used.
One should wash it with the five products of the cow.
The five products of the cow are namely milk, cream, curd, dung, and urine.
This should always be done on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month.
Before the image, one should purely and extensively arrange offerings,
lighting one hundred lamps made of cow’s ghee.
Furthermore, one should wash the vajra with fragrant water.
The practitioner who upholds this dharma shall offer their own body as a gift to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Thereafter, they shall protect their body with the mantra of the Cakravartin King.
This is to be done on the night of the fifteenth day, during the second watch.
Holding a vajra in his right hand,
he should recite the mantra single-mindedly before the image;
thereupon, flames will emerge from the vajra.
All the celestial seers, nāgas, and spirits,
together with their respective retinues, arrived at that place and escorted the practitioner of the dharma into the abode of the vidyādharas and siddhas.
He was enthroned as king.
His physical strength was equal to that of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva;
whenever he desired to go to any location, [he could do so].
Living for one great kalpa with unhindered freedom of will,
they are able to see where the Bodhisattva Maitreya preaches the True Dharma;
if they wish to seek rebirth in a particular place, they shall attain it.
One will attain rebirth with sovereign mastery as desired.
If one wishes to accomplish the rite of realgar,
take one *liang* of high-quality [realgar].
When the star of the ghosts appears, one should fast for three nights and provide a meal for the assembly of monks. Then,
with palms joined before the assembly, one should request their guidance regarding whether to proceed or remain.
If the Sangha grants permission to make offerings to the World-Honored One,
one should generate a heart of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings and light one thousand butter-lamps before that Buddha.
The mantra-holding practitioner should offer their own body to the Buddha.
Once the ritual procedure is completed,
they should make a prayer and take up the realgar while reciting the mantra.
If heat, smoke, or flames emerge,
and these three signs have appeared,
take a small amount of realgar and apply it as a mark between the eyebrows.
All devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and humans or non-humans will immediately come to serve him.
The lifespan of this mantra-holder shall be a thousand years.
If he applies [the ash] upon his forehead, the deity will not manifest its form, nor will even the heavenly gods be able to see it.
If one wishes to manifest it, one may also obtain a lifespan of three thousand years at will.
If fire is manifested, one immediately becomes a vidyādhara;
all companions shall likewise soar through the void.
Surpassing all other rishis, his lifespan shall be one kalpa.
If he relinquishes this body, he will be reborn in the Tuṣita heaven.
If he wishes to accomplish the ritual of the *daṇḍadhara* (spear-wielder), [he should proceed as follows].
One should use high-quality iron to fashion a halberd.
For one year, one should hold the halberd while reciting the mantra and construct a stupa out of sand.
Having placed food before it as an offering for sentient beings,
one sits in the lotus posture before the stupa holding a halberd in the left hand and recites the mantra;
immediately, various kinds of light rays will issue forth.
The mantra-holder immediately ascends into the void.
The hosts of Maheśvara welcome the dharma-holder,
scattering various exquisite flowers over his body as they surround him.
All other people whom he sees will together soar into the air;
that Dharma-holder shall be able to act as a great king, and the Great Maheśvara, the various devas, and the ṛṣis will all come to pay him homage; his lifespan shall last for one great kalpa.
If anyone with an evil mind should come toward one, they shall immediately fall down;
even the devas, nāgas, and ghosts cannot act with malice,
let alone ordinary people.
If one casts off this body and attains rebirth in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss,
and if one wishes to accomplish the rite for the deceased,
one should take a corpse that is free of sores or scars and has not been damaged.
One shall lie upon the ground within the maṇḍala, facing upward,
and fashion four khaṭvāṅgas using stakes made of a single-colored wood.
Bind his hands and feet.
The one who holds the mantra shall sit upon his heart.
Pound the precious substance into a powder and take a small amount of it.
Reciting the mantra one by one, he places it within the mouth of the deceased;
until the dead man opens his mouth and spits out a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*) upon his tongue.
Having obtained that jewel, he immediately becomes a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) among the vidyādharas.
Whatever weapons he desired appeared spontaneously before him;
his body emitted a radiance that illuminated more than a hundred *yi* in each of the four directions.
He possesses mastery over his lifespan;
if he should wish to become a king in another world,
he is able to relinquish his life at will.
One can be born into the stainless world.
If one wishes to accomplish the second rite for the dead,
one should follow the aforementioned instructions and take wood from a jujube tree to fashion a ritual stake.
Then, reciting the mantra over iron filings one by one,
he placed small amounts into the mouth of the deceased;
when the tongue emerged, he immediately cut it off.
His companions also ascended into the void;
they immediately obtained their wish for a lifespan of one small kalpa,
and upon passing away from this life, they were reborn in Jambudvīpa as kings.
If one wishes to accomplish the hook rite (*ākarṣaṇavidhi*),
take *kuśa* grass and fashion a hook about the size of one hand.
Wash it in the urine of five oxen.
Fast for one day and one night,
then take it up with a hook held in the hand.
Make offerings to Vajrasattva Bodhisattva by lighting one hundred butter lamps,
and first recite the Mahā-śūramgama-siddhārtha-pātra-dhāraṇī.
Having protected one's body, if one recites this mantra thereafter, it will bring about accomplishment according to the previously described wheel-method.
If one performs this for a single day, a mound of earth should be piled at the place illuminated by its radiance.
Immediately take jujube wood to fashion four stakes;
recite the mantra over each seven times and drive them into each of the four corners.
Thereby, one shall bind the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm.
During the second watch of the night, he sat in the full lotus posture and,
with single-minded devotion, made offerings to that hook,
prostrating to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
When one takes that hook and recites the mantra while holding it in hand,
all sentient beings suffering in the hells will immediately be freed from their pain.
The practitioner of the mantra shall then hear a voice and fly up into the void.
Holding this hook in hand, one shall become the king of all vidyā assemblies.
When all devas and nāgas see the mantra-holder,
they shall immediately prostrate and make offerings, and [the holder] shall have a lifespan of one great kalpa.
Upon passing away from that life,
one is immediately reborn upon the vajra-ground and beholds the vajra-realm.
If one wishes to accomplish the form [of the deity],...
If one paints a single image and fire emerges from it, one shall immediately ascend into the void and become a vidyādhara.
If one wishes to accomplish other dharmas,
one should first recite this mantra one hundred thousand times.
One must fast for one day and one night and perform a great offering.
One should take *arka* wood to kindle a fire and recite the mantra over black sesame, cow’s curd, ghee, and honey one thousand and eight times.
If one casts even a small amount into the fire, success will be attained immediately;
whatever the heart desires shall all be fulfilled.
If one wishes to subjugate Maheśvara, [one should proceed as follows].
First, one must make offerings to Maheśvara.
Seated on the southern side, perform the fire ritual by burning four substances, such as black sesame seeds and so forth.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times until it is complete.
First, one must purify and protect oneself.
Recite the mantra seven times and sprinkle water over the body;
at that moment, a sound will immediately emerge.
"You need not fear.
Maheśvara shall manifest his form immediately, and all your wishes shall be fulfilled.
If you wish to achieve mastery over Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, or others, it shall likewise be so."
One shall achieve accomplishment by performing this rite.
First, one must protect oneself.
If it is necessary to summon yakṣiṇīs—whether as mothers, sisters, or wives—[one should proceed].
Take an *aśoka* flower and recite that name;
perform the mantra over the flower three times each day until it has been recited one hundred and eight times, then burn it within the fire.
Within seven days, one will be able to arrive;
all that is wished for shall be attained.
If the mother, sister, or wife does not come within seven days, [the rite shall be performed again].
The head of that yakṣa shall split open and he will immediately be subdued.
If one wishes to summon the nāgas, one should take nāga-flowers and burn them according to the aforementioned method.
If one desires to invoke the yakṣas:
Within three months, one should take curd-rice;
at each of the three periods of the day, one shall recite the mantra one hundred and eight times until the end of the month.
On the final day, one must fast for one day and one night and make offerings to the Buddha image.
One must provide food and drink for the yakṣas and others.

Use *vāta* wood—translated as "many-rooted wood" (táng yún duō gēn mù)—for the firewood; the Tripiṭaka Master says it is produced in Guangzhou. Burn curd, clarified butter, honey, and rice within [the fire].
One who wishes to summon yakṣas through mental intention should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times over rice mixed with ghee, curd, and honey,
burning a portion of that food with each recitation.
Then the hosts of yakṣas, headed by Vaiśravaṇa, will swiftly arrive at that place.
One should take flowers of *akṣaka* wood and welcome them with these.
The yakṣas will say: "What task must we perform?"
He then said, "One yakṣa must guard my doorway every day;
whatever task you are sent to perform, you must do it immediately."
Whatever items you require shall be brought to you.
If you need a mount, you shall immediately obtain one to ride.
If you require elixirs for longevity, they shall be granted to you at once.
If one wishes to subjugate the Vajra deities,
one must first recite [the mantra] four thousand and three million two hundred thousand times,
from the first day of the twelfth month to the fifteenth day of the first month.
One must make offerings to the Buddha and provide vegetarian meals for the Sangha for twenty-one days.
One should then make a vow to dedicate the merit of these offerings to the Vajra-being.
At the second watch of that night, one should rise and sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
Within that fire, burn *agallochum* (安息香) while reciting the mantra.
The incense pellets should be the size of a *ficus religiosa* seed (*wutongzi*).
While reciting, one should visualize the Vajra deity in one's mind.
When the mantra reaches the third watch of the night, there shall be thunder and an earthquake, and various wondrous flowers shall rain down from the heavens.
Vajrapāṇi will immediately arrive, along with all the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, bodhisattvas, and others, who will come together to surround him.
The mantra-practitioner takes fragrant water and flowers, goes out to meet [the deity] with reverence and prostrations.
The Vajra then immediately asks: "What vow do you seek?"
Whatever they beg for, they shall obtain, and their lifespan shall be one kalpa.
